The SIFT gate ranks the weakest generator first

v0, v1 and v4 read against real SIFT through three lenses — neighbourhood geometry, support, and distribution. Each picks a different winner.

2026-08-13 · commit 2bf36eb · N=20000, k=100, hubness k=10, nlist=256, L2-normalized, seed 42

v0 — plain WGAN-GP, no EMA, no gated generator, no regularizer — sits closer to real SIFT than v4 on all four gate statistics. On relative contrast it is 0.13x the seed-to-seed noise floor away from real: indistinguishable.

It does this while emitting 11.8% negative components and not one exact zero, on a corpus whose defining structural fact is heavy mass at exactly zero. v4 is the only rung that reproduces that support, and it is the rung the gate ranks last.

This is a result about the gate, not an argument for shipping v0. The four statistics in src/eval/ann_difficulty.py measure neighbourhood geometry. They do not constrain support, so a generator can reproduce the geometry while placing its mass where SIFT descriptors cannot exist.

How the rungs were measured

One eda_report invocation over real sift_1m.npy and three overlays, at the canonical SIFT conditions locked in docs/datasets/sift.md. A single invocation is load-bearing: every rung shares one real-side subsample, so rung-to-rung differences carry no sampling noise of their own.

  • v0 — runs/long_baseline, 30k steps, plain WGAN-GP.
  • v1 — runs/x100k_ema_only, 100k steps, + generator EMA.
  • v4 — 30k steps, structured gated generator + log-ratio regularizer.

One confound to hold in mind: v1 is a 100k-step run while v0 and v4 are both 30k, so the v0→v1 step mixes generator EMA with 3.3x more training. Run length is an independent axis, not a variant, and nothing below separates the two.

Distance from real, in units of noise

A gap only means something against how far the statistic moves when nothing but the seed changes. That floor is per architecture and does not transfer: the MLP rungs are judged against the v0 seed-to-seed floor from docs/datasets/sift.md, v4 against the architecture-matched v3-pair spread from docs/results/v4-logratio/.

measured against the v0 seed floor measured against the v3-pair floor dashed line = 1x floor

Read the bars as “is this gap real?”, not as a ranking. Because the two floors differ, bar lengths are only comparable within a colour. For ranking closeness, use the absolute gaps below — and on those, v0 is nearest to real on every one of the four.

Each cell: value, then gap to real, then that gap in floor units. Faded cells are under 1x — within noise of real.

Both MLP rungs land within noise of real on relative contrast (0.13x and 0.30x). v4 is 7.2x out, on the far side. The log-ratio regularizer moved relative contrast away from real relative to the baseline it was built on top of.

v4’s LID number is not evidence and is not used here to rank anything. lid_reg fits the mean log-ratio profile of within-batch neighbours, which is the sufficient statistic the Hill estimator reduces to a scalar. A good lid_median was guaranteed by construction. Its 23.6x gap is reported for completeness only.

What the gate does not see

Statisticrealv0v1v4
Exact-zero fraction0.22980.00000.00000.2441
Negative fraction0.00000.11820.09830.0000
Minimum coordinate0.0000-0.1221-0.09740.0000
Duplicate rows0.000620.000000.000000.00000
Effective rank27.9927.1127.5026.81
Median 5-NN distance0.51530.50910.51400.4894

Real SIFT descriptors are non-negative and quantized: 23.0% of coordinates are exactly zero, and 0.06% of rows are exact duplicates of another row. v0 and v1 produce zero exact zeros and put roughly 10–12% of their mass below zero, down to −0.12. v4 reproduces the zero mass to within 0.014 and never goes negative.

The EMA rung moves nothing

On the gate, v0→v1 is a wash. LID moves 0.1501 (0.91x the floor), relative contrast 0.0208 (0.43x), hubness skew 0.0078 (0.13x); only IVF Gini reaches 1.77x, and Gini is the weakest discriminator of the four. Three of the four are under 1x — smaller than a reseed.

That is despite v1 carrying both generator EMA and 3.3x the training. The two are not separated here, so this says the combination lands within noise of the baseline; it does not say which of them is inert.

A panel that cannot be read, for a real reason

The relative-contrast histogram renders with its x-axis running to about 6.5×107 and every bar in the first bin. The cause is in the real set: relative contrast divides by the nearest-neighbour distance, and SIFT’s quantized lattice puts near-coincident pairs in the corpus, so a handful of real queries divide by almost zero.

Six real queries were dropped outright by survivor_mask as exact duplicates or full ties. Every synthetic rung dropped zero — no generator here produces a single exact duplicate or a fully tied neighbourhood. The median the gate uses is unaffected; only the histogram is. It is worth an issue against the panel, and it is one more instance of the report’s theme: the lattice structure is what the generators are missing.

The distribution, and why it settles nothing

Everything above is neighbourhood geometry and support. The obvious third question is whether the rungs match real SIFT as a distribution — and AGENTS.md is explicit that these are diagnostics, not the gate. Measuring them here shows why that rule exists.

A distribution diagnostic is unreadable without knowing how far real is from itself. So the corpus was split into two disjoint 20000-row halves; one is the reference every rung is scored against, and the other is scored against it the same way. That is the floor column. A rung only differs from real on a diagnostic where it clearly exceeds that floor.

Faded cells are at or near the floor — the diagnostic cannot separate that rung from a disjoint sample of real SIFT.

Three of the five diagnostics are saturated. Covariance Frobenius, MMD and the pairwise-distance histogram cannot distinguish v1 or v4 from real at all — they land between 0.5x and 1.3x the floor. On MMD, v1 (0.7x) and v4 (0.5x) score better than a real sample does.

MMD ranks v4 first. The gate ranks it last. Both numbers are correct; they are measuring different things, and only one of them is the project’s question.

This is the trap AGENTS.md names — “MMD improved, looks good” is a misreading — made concrete. It is not that these diagnostics are wrong. It is that at this point on the ladder they have no resolution left: every rung already matches real SIFT’s global second-order structure, so a scalar summarising that structure has nothing left to say.

What still separates them

Only the per-dimension marginals retain resolution: every rung clears the floor there (2.1x to 6.3x on the worst dimension), and they rank v1 best, v0 worst — a third ordering, agreeing with neither the gate nor the support check.

So the correlation panel and the marginals agree with each other and with neither of the other two lenses. Three questions, three different winners:

  • Neighbourhood geometry (the gate) → v0
  • Support (zeros, negatives, glyphs) → v4, uniquely
  • Distribution (marginals, correlation structure) → v1

No rung wins two. That is the honest summary of this ladder, and it is the reason a single scalar — whichever one — would have reported progress that is not there.

What this does not say

  • It does not say v0 is the better generator. It says four aggregate statistics do not constrain support, so a rung can win them while being obviously wrong under a panel that looks at individual vectors.
  • No gate band was set or moved. gates/sift.yaml is untouched and every band there is still null. Choosing a number is a judgement call reserved for a human.
  • IVF Gini ranks nothing. The architecture-matched floor makes it the weakest of the four discriminators, as docs/results/v4-logratio/ already found for the v3/v4 pair.
  • n=1 per rung. One seed each. Both noise floors are themselves n=2, establishing an order of magnitude and no more, and both are lower bounds — two runs at identical seed still diverge 1–8% per loss column by step 250 from nondeterministic CUDA reduction order.
  • The real-vs-real floor is one split. It resolves “saturated” from “clearly above”, which is all it is used for. It does not support fine distinctions near 1x, and the ordering of v1 and v4 on the three saturated diagnostics should not be read at all.

What follows from it

The gate needs a support check sitting beside the four statistics — exact-zero fraction and negative fraction are already computed by eda_report and would have caught v0 immediately. Whether that becomes a fifth gated statistic or a precondition is a banding decision, and belongs to a human.

Reproducing

Sampled vectors, the stock 8.5MB eda_report.html and the per-panel PNGs are on tig-gpu at /workspace/keep/sift-v0-v1-v4/eda3/. All three draws are reused verbatim from /workspace/keep/sift-ladder/.

python -m src.eval.eda_report \
    --real-path /workspace/data-cache/sift_1m.npy \
    --synthetic-path v0=samples_v0.npy \
    --synthetic-path v1=samples_v1.npy \
    --synthetic-path v4=samples_v4.npy \
    --output-dir eda3 --preprocess l2 --max-vectors 50000 \
    --ann-max-rows 20000 --ann-k 100 --ann-hub-k 10 --ivf-nlist 256 --seed 42

The distribution diagnostics and their real-vs-real floor come from dist_diag.py, committed beside this page and run as a second job at the same equal-N and seed.
